walkthroughs.body_html: Piaget poured water from a short wide beaker into a tall thin one. Preoperational children said the tall beaker had more water. Concrete operational children realised the volume was conserved. This marks logical thinking about concrete material.

Martin Hughes asked children to hide a boy doll from a policeman doll. Around 90% of 3.5-5 year olds succeeded — far better than Piaget's egocentrism claim predicted. The task made human sense, so younger children could decentre.

Piaget's ideas shaped active, discovery-based learning. Teachers use concrete materials for 7-11s and abstract problems for older students. Critics say Piaget underestimated children and ignored the role of social interaction stressed by Vygotsky.
